title: The Hidden Cost of Industry: Why Big Businesses Use So Much Public Water
subtitle: As drought impacts become more common, experts are calling for better data on how much water large companies really use.

summary.en: Large businesses in England consume massive amounts of water from the public supply, even during periods of drought. New reports suggest that industrial water use is difficult to track due to a lack of data and commercial secrecy. Regulators are now pushing for mandatory reporting to help protect national water security. Some companies argue that their usage is confidential or necessary for their operations. Improving transparency is seen as a vital step for future environmental planning.
summary.zh: 英格蘭的大型企業即使在乾旱期間，仍消耗大量的公共供水。新報告指出，由於缺乏數據與商業機密保護，工業用水量難以追蹤。監管機構目前正推動強制申報制度，以協助維護國家水資源安全。部分企業則主張其用水量屬於機密或營運必要。提升透明度被視為未來環境規劃的關鍵步驟。

paragraphs.en: In many parts of England, families are often asked to save water during dry summers. When drought conditions hit, people are told not to use garden hoses or fill swimming pools to protect the public supply. However, while households try to do their part, a new report shows that a very small number of businesses use more water every day than the needs of 10 million people combined. This situation has raised serious questions about how the country manages its most precious natural resource.
paragraphs.zh: 在英格蘭的許多地區，家庭常被要求在乾旱的夏季節約用水。當乾旱情況發生時，民眾會被告知不要使用花園水管或填滿游泳池，以保護公共供水。然而，儘管家戶努力盡一份心力，一份新的報告顯示，極少數的企業每天消耗的水量，竟超過一千萬人所需用水的總和。這種情況引發了嚴重的質疑，關於該國究竟該如何管理其最珍貴的天然資源。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian Environment, businesses across England use about 2.6 billion litres of water from the public supply every single day. This makes up roughly 30% of all public water use. Even more concerning is that two-thirds of this water is taken from areas that are already struggling with a lack of water, known as water-stressed areas. This means that while local people are asked to cut back, large industrial sites continue to use huge amounts of water without clear limits.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報環境版》（The Guardian Environment）報導，英格蘭各地的企業每天從公共供水系統中消耗約二十六億公升的水，這大約佔了所有公共用水量的百分之三十。更令人擔憂的是，其中三分之二的水源來自已經面臨缺水困境的地區，也就是所謂的「缺水壓力區」。這意味著當當地民眾被要求節約用水時，大型工業場所卻能持續使用巨量的水，且沒有明確的限制。

paragraphs.en: Tracking exactly how much water these companies use is surprisingly difficult. The Guardian Environment reports that regulators are frustrated by a lack of clear data and what they call “commercial secrecy.” Because many companies do not want their private business information to become public, it is hard for the government to plan for the future. Without accurate information, it is impossible to know if there will be enough water for everyone as the population grows and the climate changes.
paragraphs.zh: 追蹤這些企業確切的用水量出奇地困難。《衛報環境版》報導指出，監管機構對於缺乏明確數據以及所謂的「商業機密」感到挫折。由於許多公司不希望其私人商業資訊公開，導致政府難以進行未來規劃。在缺乏準確資訊的情況下，隨著人口增長與氣候變遷，根本無法得知未來是否會有足夠的水供所有人使用。

paragraphs.en: One of the biggest users of the public water supply is the ExxonMobil refinery in Southampton. Mosl, the organization that manages the business water market in England, pointed to this site as an example of high water waste that is not discouraged by current government rules. In written evidence to a House of Lords committee, Mosl suggested that the current system does not give companies enough reason to save water. However, ExxonMobil has disputed these figures, stating that its water use is commercially confidential. The company also explained that most of the water it takes is used for cooling systems that are necessary for its operations, and that it cannot easily reduce this usage without shutting down parts of its factory.
paragraphs.zh: 公共供水系統的最大使用者之一是位於南安普敦（Southampton）的艾克森美孚（ExxonMobil）煉油廠。負責管理英格蘭商業用水市場的組織 Mosl 指出，該廠是目前政府法規未能遏止高耗水浪費的一個例子。在提交給上議院委員會的書面證據中，Mosl 表示現行制度並未給予企業足夠的節水誘因。然而，艾克森美孚對這些數據提出異議，聲稱其用水量屬於商業機密。該公司並解釋，其取用的大部分水是用於營運所需的冷卻系統，若不關閉部分工廠，很難輕易減少用水量。

paragraphs.en: This lack of transparency is not just a problem for one company. The Guardian Environment notes that one in ten businesses in England do not even have a meter to measure how much water they use. Of the businesses that do have meters, only a small number use “smart meters”—devices that send real-time data to water companies. This means that for a large portion of the business sector, the exact amount of water being taken from the public supply remains a mystery.
paragraphs.zh: 這種缺乏透明度的問題並非單一公司所獨有。《衛報環境版》指出，英格蘭每十家企業中，就有一家甚至沒有安裝測量用水量的水表。而在有安裝水表的企業中，僅有少數使用能將即時數據傳送給供水公司的「智慧水表」。這意味著對於商業領域的很大一部分而言，從公共供水系統中取用的確切水量仍然是一個謎。

paragraphs.en: Sarah McMath, the chief executive of Mosl, told a House of Lords committee that even government departments struggle to get the information they need. She explained that when the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) or the Environment Agency asks for data, Mosl often has to create a special agreement just to share it. This slow process makes it very difficult for the government to make quick decisions about how to protect the environment or support society during a water crisis.
paragraphs.zh: Mosl 的執行長莎拉·麥克馬斯（Sarah McMath）向上議院委員會表示，即使是政府部門也難以取得所需的資訊。她解釋說，當環境、食品暨農村事務部（Defra）或環境署（Environment Agency）要求數據時，Mosl 往往必須簽署特別協議才能分享。這種緩慢的流程，使得政府在面對水資源危機時，很難針對如何保護環境或支援社會做出快速決策。

paragraphs.en: To solve this, the Environment Agency and the water regulator, Ofwat, are now calling for mandatory reporting. This would mean that all large businesses would be required by law to report how much water they use now and how much they expect to use in the future. By making this information public, regulators hope to improve national water security—a state where there is enough clean water for everyone to live and work safely.
paragraphs.zh: 為了改善此一問題，環境署與水務監管機構 Ofwat 正呼籲實施強制申報制度。這意味著所有大型企業將依法被要求申報目前的用水量，以及預計未來的用水需求。透過公開這些資訊，監管機構希望提升國家水資源安全，即確保每個人都能在安全的情況下獲得足夠的乾淨用水以供生活與工作。

paragraphs.en: As the climate continues to change, the pressure on water supplies will likely increase. Experts believe that the current system of “commercial secrecy” is no longer acceptable when the environment is at risk. By moving toward a system of open data and mandatory reporting, the government hopes to ensure that industrial growth does not come at the cost of the public’s basic needs. For now, the debate continues over how to balance the needs of big business with the urgent need to protect the water that everyone relies on.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著氣候持續變遷，水資源供應的壓力可能會日益增加。專家認為，當環境面臨風險時，現行的「商業機密」制度已不再適用。透過轉向公開數據與強制申報的制度，政府希望確保工業成長不會以犧牲大眾的基本需求為代價。目前，關於如何在大型企業的需求與每個人都依賴的水資源保護迫切性之間取得平衡，相關辯論仍在持續進行。

sources.name: The Guardian Environment
sources.title: Revealed: how companies ‘secretly’ use billions of litres of public water in drought-hit England

quiz.question: According to the article, what is the current status of water usage monitoring for businesses in England?

options.A: All businesses are required to install smart meters to ensure real-time data reporting.
options.B: A significant number of businesses lack water meters entirely, making their usage unknown.
options.C: The government has successfully forced all large industrial sites to disclose their exact water intake.
options.D: Most businesses voluntarily report their water usage to the Environment Agency to avoid fines.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第五段，文中明確提到「one in ten businesses in England do not even have a meter」，且只有少數企業使用智慧水表，這證實了許多企業的用水量完全無法測量。選項 A 錯誤，因為只有少數企業使用智慧水表；選項 C 錯誤，因為目前仍存在「商業機密」問題，政府難以取得數據；選項 D 錯誤，文中並未提到企業是「自願」報告，反而是因為缺乏透明度而受到監管機構的批評。

quiz.question: What can be inferred about the relationship between industrial water use and public water restrictions?

options.A: Industrial sites are the primary reason why households are asked to stop using garden hoses.
options.B: The government prioritizes industrial growth over the needs of households during drought conditions.
options.C: There is a disconnect between the sacrifices expected of the public and the oversight of industrial water consumption.
options.D: Large businesses are already reducing their water usage as much as possible to help the public.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。文章第一段與第二段對比了家庭被要求節水（禁止使用水管、泳池）與大型工業區在缺水地區大量用水卻無明確限制的現狀。這暗示了兩者之間存在管理上的落差與不公平。選項 A 過度推論，文中未指明工業是導致家庭禁水的唯一原因；選項 B 雖然反映了現狀，但文章重點在於「缺乏透明度」而非政府刻意偏袒；選項 D 與文章內容矛盾，Mosl 指出企業缺乏節水的誘因。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'disputed' mean as it is used in the context of ExxonMobil?

options.A: Argued against or challenged the accuracy of information.
options.B: Accepted the findings but refused to change operations.
options.C: Requested more time to verify the provided data.
options.D: Ignored the report because it came from an unreliable source.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在第四段中，Mosl 提出 ExxonMobil 浪費水，而 ExxonMobil 對此作出了回應，稱其用水數據是商業機密，並解釋了用水原因。由此可知，ExxonMobil 是在「質疑」或「反駁」Mosl 所提出的數據準確性或解讀方式。選項 B 錯誤，因為該公司並未接受這些指控；選項 C 與 D 並未在文中體現，該公司是採取了防禦性的回應態度。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding water management in England?

options.A: The government needs to increase taxes on businesses that use too much water.
options.B: Climate change is the only factor responsible for the current water crisis in England.
options.C: ExxonMobil is solely responsible for the water shortages currently affecting the country.
options.D: Improved transparency and mandatory reporting are needed to balance industrial water use with public needs.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。本文的核心論點在於探討工業用水缺乏透明度，導致政府難以管理資源。文章最後兩段明確指出，為了應對氣候變遷與資源壓力，監管機構正推動「強制報告制度（mandatory reporting）」與「公開數據」，以確保工業發展不會犧牲公眾的基本需求。選項 A 未在文中提及；選項 B 過於簡化，忽略了管理體系的問題；選項 C 錯誤，ExxonMobil 僅是一個案例，而非問題的全部。
